evidence.title: NASA and ESA outline Mars Sample Return campaign with launches in 2026
evidence.snippet: NASA and ESA plan to launch the Mars Sample Return lander and Earth Return Orbiter in 2026, bringing Perseverance's samples back to Earth in the early 2030s.

evidence.title: KB-030: NASA's Mars Sample Return has been delayed and restructured; no 2026 launch
evidence.snippet: NASA's Mars Sample Return (MSR) has not launched. The original plan targeted launches around 2026 with samples back in the early 2030s, but after an independent review warned costs could reach $11 billion, NASA in January 2025 outlined two cheaper architectures with launches around 2030-2031 and Earth return between 2035 and 2039. A decision between them was deferred to mid-2026, and the President's FY2026 budget request proposed cancelling the program.
